LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_LookBack_Text: The day after the eclipse, the noon light stands white over {HOME} and the heat comes down hard: the shadows don't move, and the air shimmers off every stone. Those out of doors have stopped to shade their eyes.
LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_Saw_LookBack: {WHO} saw the noon light stand white over {HOME} the day after the eclipse, and the shadows not move.
LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_Fruit_Text: {COUNT} of {HOME} walked out into the noon sun by the fields and ate the first fruit of the year there, asking for nothing.
LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_Fruit_TextNone: {COUNT} of {HOME} walked out into the noon sun by the fields and stood there together a while; there was no fresh fruit in the stores to eat.
LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_Book_Fruit: The first fruit of the year was eaten out under the noon sun by {COUNT} of us, asking for nothing.
LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_Dawn_Text: After the longest night, {COUNT} of {HOME} walked out to the east side and stood facing the sunrise, and it came up gold and lay on them a while.
LanguageData.CC_GodHelios_Saw_Dawn: {COUNT} of {HOME} stood facing the sunrise after the longest night, and it lay on them gold a while.
